endorsement_id: <END-NNNN, issued by the Project Book on ATTACH kind endorsement>
revision_id: <Rnn — the exact revision the signature covers; the only revision that may be marked consultant-endorsed>
revision_sha256: <SHA-256 of the registered revision's original bytes>
sha256: <SHA-256 of the received signed original, byte-for-byte, as received>
attachment_id: <ATT-NNNN of the stored signed original / letter>
signer: <person who signed, as named on the document>
date: <YYYY-MM-DD on the signature or covering letter>
conditions: <conditions attached to the endorsement, verbatim or by reference to the letter; empty string if none>
scope: <floors, systems, disciplines and package covered, e.g. L22 CHW or S9 package>
covering_letter_ref: <reference to the covering letter or confirmation email (attachment id or filename)>

package_manifest.document_id: <DOC-<DISC>-<NNNN> of each file in a package signature, one line per signed file>
package_manifest.verified: <true when the line matches the registered revision; any false line keeps status 'to be confirmed'>

received_date: <YYYY-MM-DD received; register within one working day (company target)>
registered_by: <PM or discipline lead who registered it>
note: Covers this revision_id only; a later revision never inherits it. Originals stay byte-for-byte unchanged; previews and OCR are linked copies. A scanned signature is not a verified digital signature: digital_signature_verified stays false unless a digital signature was actually verified. Endorsement, construction issue and as-built acceptance are three separate records; none of them is a technical PASS. Status is 'to be confirmed' while the manifest or scope is unclear, and the revision is then not marked endorsed.
